thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] 14:12 UTC — Service: inference-api /v1/generate — error rate spike >8% in us-west-2. Paging oncall @oncall-alex

oncall-alex: I'm on it, ack. starting diagnostics and checking recent deploys.

oncall-alex: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-17T14:12:22Z ERROR request_handler: grpc: connection reset by peer
2026-03-17T14:12:24Z WARN autoscaler: scale_down_eviction node-gpu-5
2026-03-17T14:12:25Z ERROR runtime: OOM during attention kernel
```

sre-maya: I see NACKs and OOM evictions on node-gpu-5. Autoscaler oscillation after a burst. Manually pinning pool to 3 nodes to stop thrash.

eng-manager-luca: thanks. CS, can you draft a short statuspage blurb + customer email template? Need something customer-facing we can send in 10–15m.

cs-jordan: Drafting now — cc @prod-ops-lee for technical accuracy.

cs-jordan: STATUSPAGE DRAFT:
```
Title: Degraded performance for text-generation in us-west-2
Impact: Some requests to the /v1/generate endpoint returned errors or experienced elevated latency between 14:10–14:31 UTC.
Current status: Mitigated — traffic routed to fallback model and node pool pinned.
Next update: Final update with timeline and mitigations in ~1-2 hours.
```

prod-ops-lee: Suggest adding: "We routed a subset of traffic to model-smaller-v2 (approx -20% throughput) to reduce failures. No customer data was exposed." Also include ETA for full restoration.

acme-support: thanks for the heads up. Can you share a compact timeline and whether in-flight requests were lost? Our customers reported 5xx on some jobs.

oncall-alex: timeline: issue started ~14:10 UTC after a sudden ingest burst. Mitigation started 14:16 UTC (manual pin + fallback routing). Stabilized at 14:31 UTC. We're still validating exact customer-level failure counts; initial estimate: ~0.7% of requests in the window returned 5xx.

sre-maya: Short RCA (initial): combination of aggressive scale-down logic + kernel memory pressure for long-sequence inputs. Autoscaler removed nodes too quickly under bursty load and the runtime hit OOM in the attention kernel.

eng-manager-luca: Action items (owners):
- Disable aggressive scale-down for autoscaler during high-burst windows — @eng-manager-luca
- Add admission control for extremely long sequences + memory guard rails in kernel — @sre-maya
- Ship fallback routing policy improvements and HA testing — @prod-ops-lee
- Customer communications and SLA credit estimate — @cs-jordan

eng-manager-luca: Preliminary SLA credit estimate: potential 6–8 hours of impacted availability for customers within the affected window; final calc pending verification of per-customer failure counts.

cs-jordan: CUSTOMER EMAIL DRAFT:
```
Hi Team,

We want to apologize for the disruption to text generation in us-west-2 on 2026-03-17 between 14:10–14:31 UTC. During this period some requests to /v1/generate returned errors or experienced increased latency.

What happened: A scaling oscillation combined with memory pressure for long-sequence workloads caused a subset of GPU workers to fail and reject requests.

What we did: We pinned the node pool to stop autoscaler thrash, routed traffic to a compatible fallback model, and stabilized service by 14:31 UTC.

Impact: Initial analysis shows ~0.7% of requests in the window returned 5xx. We are validating the full customer list and will share a final impact table.

Next steps: Technical fixes (admission checks, memory guard rails) scheduled and tracked in RFC/PR. We will provide a formal RCA by EOD tomorrow and propose SLA credit where appropriate.

If you'd like a 1:1 to discuss impact for your account, please let us know.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Inference team
```

prod-ops-lee: addendum — we'll include links to the postmortem and PRs once created. Recommending a follow-up maintenance window next week to roll kernel memory fixes and run burst tests.

oncall-alex: resolving on-call mitigations now. Leaving follow-ups for SRE/eng. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] 14:31 UTC — Traffic stabilized; fallback routing active; node pool pinned.

cs-jordan: Sending the customer note to Acme now, will attach the above timeline and a contact for 1:1.

acme-support: appreciate the clear timeline. Please share the final RCA and any tickets for preventive work.

eng-manager-luca: We'll publish the full RCA by EOD tomorrow. It will include root cause analysis, PR links, regression tests added, and owners for each action.

sre-maya: Created internal issue #4523 and PR draft for admission checks + memory guard rails. Baseline tests for long-sequence workloads in progress.

cs-jordan: Logged the customer follow-up in CRM and scheduled a 1:1 with Acme for 15:00 UTC tomorrow to review impact and credits.

oncall-alex: closing thread from on-call side. Ping if anything else surfaces.
